sourcedFrom: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) (2013)
cleanIntro: The Affinity is an inertia-driven semi-auto: there is no gas system to foul, and the whole action runs on a stiff bolt blow back spring sitting between the bolt and its rotating locking head. That one spring is why the strip has a hard rule attached to it — reassembled without it, or with it in the wrong place, the gun can fire as the bolt closes. Franchi's own book is scoped to the Affinity range rather than to one generation, and it is written for a right-handed gun.

steps.title: What this book covers, and which hand it is written for
steps.action: Two bounds to know before you start. Franchi wrote this manual for the Affinity range of semi-automatic shotguns rather than for one model year, and every illustration and description in it assumes a right-handed gun. If yours is a left-handed Affinity, the parts are mirrored and the directions in the text are not.
steps.prose: Neither bound changes the mechanism. They change which side of the receiver you are looking at and how much the book can tell you about your particular variant.
steps.aside: The scope sentence reads: "– Franchi has issued this manual to present the specific qualities of AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns."
steps.quote: – Illustrations and descriptions indicated in this manual refer to the RIGHT-HANDED VERSION firearm.
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Introduction, printed p.23

steps.title: Ammunition is set by the gauge marked on the gun
steps.action: Check the gauge and chamber length stamped on the barrel and match your shells to it. Franchi states that the shotgun takes any cartridge in the gauge marked on the firearm within C.I.P. limits, and that the gun needs no adjustment for different loads — but it draws a hard line at case length.
steps.prose: An inertia gun does need enough recoil to cycle. Franchi's own condition is cartridges that deliver enough blow back to complete the cycle, which is why very light target loads can short-stroke a new gun before it is run in.
steps.quote: Affinity shotguns can use all cartridges in the gauge indicated on the firearm, in compliance with the C.I.P.
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Ammunition, printed p.25
steps.warn: Do not use cartridges with a case longer than the chamber!

steps.title: Unload the chamber, then the magazine, one shell at a time
steps.action: Safety on, muzzle safe. Open the bolt — that takes the shell out of the chamber — then release the bolt. Turn the gun over, push the carrier in and press the front of the carrier latch with your index finger: the first shell comes out of the magazine. Press the latch again for each remaining shell until the tube is empty.
steps.prose: The safety is a crossbolt button and the tell is the red ring: visible means NOT safe. Check the ring rather than the button's position.
steps.quote: Always keep the firearm with the safety catch engaged and the barrel pointed in a safe direction. Proceed as follows. – Open the bolt.
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Unloading the Firearm, printed p.28
steps.warn: SAFETY CATCH NOT INSERTED: red ring VISIBLE. Engaged means the red ring is NOT visible.

steps.title: Prove chamber, carrier and magazine are all empty
steps.action: Before a single part comes off, verify all three: chamber, carrier and magazine tube. Franchi asks for this as its own step at the head of the strip, separately from the unloading procedure, because a shell can still be sitting on the carrier after the tube reads empty.
steps.prose: Franchi also asks you to lay out a clean cloth and place the parts down in the order they came off. On this gun that is genuinely useful — the bolt breaks into five small pieces.
steps.quote: Always ensure that the chamber, carrier and magazine are completely empty
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Disassembling the Firearm for Maintenance, printed p.29
steps.warn: – Before performing any intervention on the firearm, ensure that both chamber and magazine are empty.

steps.title: Fore-end cap off, barrel unit off the magazine tube
steps.action: Unscrew the fore-end cap from the end of the magazine tube, then draw the barrel-breech-fore-end unit forward off the tube as one piece. That is the gun in its two shipped halves: barrel unit, and stock-breech-bolt unit.
steps.prose: It is the same joint the gun was shipped in — Franchi delivers it as these two units in the box. If the barrel will not come, the cap is still catching a thread.
steps.quote: 1. Loosen the fore-end cap (figure 21). 2. Pull off the barrel-breech-fore-end cap
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Disassembling the Firearm for Maintenance, steps 1–2, printed p.29

steps.title: Bolt handle out, then the bolt-swivel-recoil spring unit
steps.action: Hold the stock-breech-bolt unit and take the bolt back to the open position until it couples. Pull the bolt handle straight out. Then hold the bolt by its swivel, press the carrier control button, and draw the bolt-swivel-recoil spring unit out of the breech as one assembly.
steps.prose: If the bolt will not stay coupled open, work the cartridge drop lever and try again. Handle the unit out carefully — it is three parts held together only by your grip.
steps.caution: Handle the unit with care and be sure not to drop any components.
steps.quote: 4. Extract the bolt handle (figure 25). 5. Hold the bolt using the swivel (figure
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Disassembling the Firearm for Maintenance, steps 4–5, printed p.29

steps.title: Firing pin out — retaining pin first
steps.action: Working on the bolt alone now. Hold the firing pin in place with a finger and drive out the firing pin retaining pin, then let the firing pin and its spring come out of the bolt body.
steps.prose: Hold the pin before you push the retainer. It is spring-loaded and it will launch if you let go of it at the wrong moment.
steps.aside: The next step reads: "2. Remove the firing pin and its relative spring (figure 30)."
steps.quote: 1. Hold the firing pin and remove the firing retaining pin (figure 29).
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Disassembling the Firearm for Maintenance, printed p.29

steps.title: Locking head off, and the blow back spring out
steps.action: Push the locking head rotating pin out of its housing, lift the bolt locking head off the bolt, and take the bolt blow back spring out of its seat. Those three parts are the inertia system — the spring is the one everything else depends on.
steps.prose: Note where the spring sits: between the locking head and the bolt body. That position is the whole point, and it is the thing to get right on the way back.
steps.quote: 3. Remove the locking head rotating pin from its housing (figure 31).
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Disassembling the Firearm for Maintenance, printed p.29
steps.warn: Always place the bolt blow back spring between the locking head and the bolt, to avoid a shot being fired when closing the bolt.

steps.title: Trigger guard unit out — stop plug, then slide it forward
steps.action: Use the end of the firing pin or a suitable punch to push the trigger guard stop plug out of the stock-breech unit from either side. Then press the carrier control button and slide the whole trigger guard unit forward and out.
steps.prose: With that out the gun is fully disassembled as far as Franchi documents it. Everything beyond this point the book explicitly tells you not to take apart.
steps.caution: Do not try to disassemble parts or components of the firearm if not specified in the manual, and do not attempt to modify or repair them.
steps.quote: 2. Press the carrier control button and slide the trigger guard unit forwards (figure 35).
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Disassembling the Firearm for Maintenance, printed p.29

steps.title: Barrel — leave the choke IN while you clean it
steps.action: Clean the bore with a brush or a cloth soaked in a non-corrosive solvent to lift the combustion residue, then wipe it out with a clean cloth and finish with a cloth lightly wetted with oil. Leave the choke tube installed the whole time: taking it out first lets residue pack into the choke threads inside the barrel, where it is far harder to get at.
steps.prose: The bores are chrome plated, so they take solvent well and do not need aggressive work. It is the choke threads that punish shortcuts.
steps.aside: The same section reads: "When cleaning the barrel, leave the choke installed to prevent residues building up in its connection threads inside the barrel."
steps.quote: – Clean the barrel with a brush or with a cloth soaked in a special non-corrosive solvent, to remove combustion residues.
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Maintenance, printed p.29

steps.title: Every component cleaned, checked, then oiled thinly
steps.action: Clean each part and check it is undamaged while it is in your hand — this is the inspection, not just the cleaning. Use a non-corrosive solvent on anything showing combustion residue and dry it with a clean cloth. Then lubricate everything with a thin coat of oil and no more than that.
steps.prose: Franchi is blunt that too much oil causes damage or malfunctions on this action. An inertia gun is not helped by a wet receiver; it is slowed by one.
steps.aside: The section opens: "MAINTENANCE The Franchi semi-automatic shotgun does not require special maintenance procedures."
steps.quote: – Carefully lubricate all the components with a thin coat of oil.
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Maintenance, printed p.30

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrel unit is off, the bolt is out and broken down to firing pin, locking head and blow back spring, and the trigger guard unit is out of the receiver. That is everything Franchi publishes. The book's own limit is explicit: only experienced owners familiar with the gun should strip it, nothing outside the documented steps comes apart, and repairs go to an authorised dealer.
steps.prose: Lay the parts out in the order they came off. The bolt goes back in a specific order, and the blow back spring has a safety consequence if it is wrong.
steps.quote: ONLY experienced people should strip the shotgun, provided they are familiar with it.
steps.cite: AFFINITY semiautomatic shotguns — owner's manual (2013) — 2013 multi-language edition (EN block printed pp.23–34) — Suggestions for Maintenance, printed p.28

deepAbsentReason: Franchi publishes no procedure deeper than the strip above, and says so twice in its own words: 'Do not try to disassemble parts or components of the firearm if not specified in paragraph "Dismounting the firearm for maintenance"' and 'Do not attempt to modify or repair the components of the firearm. For help, contact an authorised dealer or qualified personnel.' The documented strip already reaches the trigger guard unit and the individual bolt components — firing pin, spring, retaining pin, locking head, rotating pin and blow back spring — so there is no further owner-level teardown to publish. There is no trigger-group internals procedure, no carrier or carrier-latch removal, no magazine tube or spring procedure and no stock removal anywhere in the English block (printed pp.23–34), and no other Franchi document exists to draw one from: Franchi's manuals index publishes three PDFs in total, the other two being the Instinct over-under and the Momentum bolt-action. Nothing beyond what the book prints has been invented.

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHOKE
tasks: Leave the choke tube INSTALLED while cleaning the bore
Brush or solvent-soaked cloth with a non-corrosive solvent to lift combustion residue
Wipe the bore out with a clean cloth, then a cloth lightly wetted with oil
Bores are chrome plated — no aggressive abrasives needed

cleaning.name: BOLT & LOCKING HEAD
tasks: Clean the firing pin, its spring, the locking head and the rotating pin individually
Check the blow back spring is undamaged before it goes back
Check the reference line on the end of the rotating pin is intact — it is the alignment mark
Thin coat of oil only; excess oil causes malfunctions on an inertia action

cleaning.name: BREECH & TRIGGER GUARD UNIT
tasks: Clean residue from the breech guides and the carrier
Clean the trigger guard unit externally and check it for damage
Do not disassemble anything not named in the manual's own strip
Repairs and modifications go to an authorised dealer, not the bench

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE & RECOIL SPRING
tasks: Wipe the outside of the magazine tube where the recoil spring and barrel ring ride
Check the recoil spring is undamaged and seats on the tube
Clean the fore-end cap threads at the end of the tube
Light oil on the tube, then wipe the excess off

reassembly: Cock the trigger unit hammer, press the carrier control button and insert the trigger guard unit into the breech, then check it is wedged against the back end of the breech and fit its stop plug from either side.
Place the bolt blow back spring in its housing — always between the locking head and the bolt, or the gun can fire as the bolt closes.
Fit the bolt locking head so the hole in its stem lines up with the slot in the bolt; the inclined surfaces on the stem must not be visible once it is seated.
Pass the locking head rotating pin through the bolt slot into the hole in the locking head stem, with the reference line on the pin's end visible and aligned with the bolt's long axis.
Put the firing pin and its spring into the bolt hole — check the spring is there — and fit the firing pin retaining pin to lock it.
Place the recoil spring on the magazine tube, join the bolt unit to the swivel, and with the gun nearly vertical set the swivel-bolt unit into the breech guides.
Pull the locking head slightly back and insert the bolt handle into its housing in the bolt.

Refit the barrel-breech-fore-end unit onto the magazine tube with the bolt held open, push the barrel fully home until it clicks, tighten the fore-end cap, then press the control button to close the bolt.
fncheck: With the gun empty, open and close the bolt several times and confirm it runs freely, locks open and closes fully — Franchi asks for this specifically as the last assembly step. Check the fore-end edge sits perfectly in the breech housing and that NONE of the chrome barrel extension is visible at the front of the breech; if any chrome shows, the barrel is not fully home. Confirm the fore-end cap is tight against the barrel and fore-end. Then check the safety: red ring visible means the gun will fire, red ring hidden means it will not, and the trigger must not release the hammer with the ring hidden. Finally check the red point on the cartridge drop lever shows when the hammer is cocked.
